message.content:
You are synthesizing 8 domain experts who independently designed the learning loop, scenario/objective acceptance criteria, and sufficiency-vs-in-person analysis for a verbal Slovenian-tutor app. The reader is the app's builder. They want a SYNTHESIZED, DECISIVE, IMMEDIATELY ACTIONABLE result — not a menu. Prioritize the most effective + most reproducible methods. Distinguish buildable-now (existing tools: per-turn LLM prompt, deterministic objective state machine, objective record shape, scenario/objective ordering, story preview, practice mode, takeaway, userVerbatim+userSaid per turn, cached replayable audio, pre-generated images) from net-new (cross-session learner model, pronunciation scoring, barge-in, etc.).

App tools recap (design within these): verbal push-to-talk; one multimodal model returns per turn {userVerbatim (raw ASR), userSaid (English gloss), tutorReply (short, Slovenian only), correction (English UI note, never spoken), objectiveProgress[] (completed/attempted), focusObjectiveId}; native TTS streamed + cached + replayable; objectives = ordered {targetSL canonical phrase, label, hintEN common-error note} with deterministic pending→recast→completed and a 14-turn cap; optional ≤5-sentence narrated visual+audio story (one frame/objective + all-in scene); free practice mode (hear canonical / record self / compare); captured replayable runs; shared objective ids reuse audio across scenarios.

=== THE 8 EXPERT OUTPUTS (condensed faithfully; every concrete recommendation preserved) ===

[A1 — SLA acquisition researcher]
LOOP: pushed output of chunks under communicative pressure → recast → forced re-production of corrected form on a LATER turn (highest-value mechanic). Preview = comprehensible-input priming, silent-input only, NO grammar rules. Practice mode before live turn for objectives ≥4 syllables. Per-turn prompt enforces turn policy: tutorReply is ONE short Slovenian utterance that REQUIRES a Slovenian response (ends in a question/slot to fill — negotiation of meaning); recast embeds corrected form conversationally ("Ah, dve kavi?"), English correction field UI-only; focusObjectiveId advances in fixed order and the prompt ELICITS the next objective's function. Deterministic rule to ADD: a recast (◐) objective is marked ● only when the learner reproduces the corrected form correctly on a later turn (forced uptake). Session: greeting→core→closing, cap 14; if still ◐ at cap, takeaway flags "say it once more" and it becomes objective #1 on re-run (cheap spaced practice).
SCENARIO RUBRIC: one real bounded transaction ≤14 turns; 4-7 objectives ordered as a real script; every objective functionally elicitable by the persona (a natural tutor question makes the target the obvious answer); ≥1 objective forces negotiation (clarification/quantity/substitution), not pure recitation; reuse shared objectives by same id/audio; story ≤5 sentences one frame/objective + all-in scene; end state = a communicative success the learner can picture doing tomorrow. Mediocre tells: isolated vocab, order not mirroring real interaction, tutor must lecture to elicit, completion requires reading.
OBJECTIVE RUBRIC: targetSL is a whole formulaic chunk (2-6 words) doing a communicative job (not a lemma); high surrender value (reused across situations); hintEN names the specific predictable error; elicitable by a single question; completion judged on communicative+formal correctness of the chunk (not the English gloss); recast echoed in-character + a slot to reuse it; must resurface to complete.
SUFFICIENCY: already beats chit-chat on (guaranteed pushed output, systematic recast-then-reuse, infinite free replay). Gaps ranked: (1) NO cross-session spacing/retrieval — net-new, highest; even crude "seen N days ago → resurface as objective #1" beats nothing. (2) single canonical phrase brittle → accepted-variant set (buildable). (3) no fluency/automatization pressure → optional "second lap" re-run faster (buildable). (4) no productive recombination → final "mix" objective combining two earlier chunks (net-new). (5) no pronunciation feedback (net-new).
TOP MOVES: forced-uptake rule in state machine; turn policy in prompt (every reply ends in an elicitation, recasts in-character, never lecture); accepted-variant sets; resurface-first re-run; chunk-not-word authoring audit.
COUNTER: input-primacy (Krashen) — pushing accuracy/correction too early raises anxiety & suppresses willingness to communicate; the scarce resource (cheap replayable native audio) might be better spent on much more input.

[A2 — working speaking tutor / polyglot]
LOOP: run story preview (5 frames, SL only, autoplay, no quiz — input priming). Front-load greeting + one content word; first objective completable in one attempt = early win. Per-turn prompt persona: max 8 words/tutor turn, never explain grammar in character, ALWAYS leave a gap; if learner silent/garbage twice, restate simpler not longer. CIRCLING LADDER encoded as IF/THEN rules (deterministic, not "use circling"): new objective → yes/no ("Kavo?"); attempted-but-wrong → either/or ("Kavo ali čaj?"); still failing → question-word ("Kaj želite?"); once completed → return 2 turns later with a single yes/no check (graduated recall). RECAST: tutor's NEXT line naturally models the correct form ("Ah, kavo! Seveda."), never meta-comment; if prior turn had a correction, open the reply by modeling the target in context. State: completed ONLY if produced on a turn AFTER the recast (no lucky single-turn). At turn 10 the prompt shifts to "we're finishing — guide to complete remaining"; no new ground after turn 10. Takeaway: full phrases only, with audio.
SCENARIO RUBRIC: completable in 14 turns by a zero-Slovenian adult (paper-test it before building); single transaction with clear open/close arc; 4-6 objectives, no objective >2 new words at once; ordered greeting→noun→quantity/modifier→response-to-question→closing; shared ids for recurring phrases; story frames map 1:1 to objectives (not grammar points); no "understand X" objectives; a naive prompt-follower (no Slovenian) could complete it by circling logic alone.
OBJECTIVE RUBRIC: targetSL is a complete utterance a native would actually say (not a conjugation pattern); completable in isolation (no prior objective's output required as input); hintEN names ONE specific error; completion = exact or phonetically-close match; recast uses a DIFFERENT elicitation frame (not the same question louder); resurfaces ≥1x post-completion (graduated recall at turn+2); shared audio reused.
SUFFICIENCY gaps: (1) silence pressure: 4s silence → re-elicit (buildable). (2) brittle acceptance → accept ±1 word-order variation + 2-3 alternates/objective (buildable). (3) cross-session memory + a 3-turn returning-learner warm-up of last session's takeaway (net-new). (4) pronunciation: prompt the learner to compare their playback to native, retry (low-tech, buildable). (5) scenario variety incl. registers (buildable).
TOP MOVES: encode circling ladder as IF/THEN; front-load story preview; recast-by-modeling not correction; graduated-recall ping at turn+2; ±1 alternate acceptance.
COUNTER: deterministic circling ladders → learners good at THIS app's question patterns, brittle elsewhere ("Kavo ali čaj?" 3x then freeze at "Kaj vam dam?"); must rotate elicitation phrasing + scenario variety or fluency is stimulus-response illusion.

[A3 — adult expat who learned Slovenian]
LOOP: preview = emotional calibration (feel the register/mood), one frame/objective, SL read aloud, no English. In the turn loop, correction appears SILENT in peripheral vision, tutor does NOT break character — the world keeps moving whether or not you caught the grammar (builds real tolerance). Dot fills, no celebration noise. Takeaway: pause to hear each correct phrase once, cleanly. Across runs: objectives should GROW the scenario — run1 survive ordering, run2 add paying, run3 add small talk.
SCENARIO RUBRIC: a transaction you WILL face within 2 weeks; tutor register matches reality (not artificially slow/patient); objectives ordered by what breaks down first (not "logical" grammar sequence); phrases you'd actually say; a cultural landmine covered (e.g. "prosim" = please AND you're-welcome AND "what?"); completable while standing at a counter slightly panicked; story grounded in the real physical space; max 6 objectives.
OBJECTIVE RUBRIC: real phrase not textbook; hintEN names the SPECIFIC error ("beginners say 'kava'; it's 'kavo', accusative after 'bi'"); ≤~8 syllables (holdable in working memory under stress); exactly one natural moment where it's the thing to say; recast shows the correct form; PRACTICE audio at NATURAL speed not slowed (slowed builds wrong motor habits).
SUFFICIENCY (ranked by how much it would've helped): (1) correction that names the EXACT error — buildable; the most valuable thing the tool can do that human chit-chat never did reliably. (2) graduated difficulty within the same scenario across runs — buildable. (3) register variation: same objective polite-stranger vs friend — buildable. (4) cross-session "you got this right last week" — net-new, hugely motivating. (5) pronunciation scoring (č/š/ž) — net-new.
TOP MOVES: nail the hintEN exact-error field; tutor stays in character through corrections; scenario sequencing across runs (harder on return); short phrases, accusative-first; takeaway replayable OFFLINE (rehearse on the walk before going in).
COUNTER: optimizes the bounded counter transaction (overweighted because that's where humiliation was most visible); real acquisition is also ambient/low-stakes; learner can order coffee flawlessly and still be lost when a real person responds off-script.

[A4 — cognitive scientist of memory/retrieval]
LOOP (with numbers): require 3 successful UNAIDED retrievals at expanding spacing before "completed" (1 is too noisy). Lags measured in intervening turns ≈ 0, ≥2, ≥4 (expanding). Engine keeps per-objective nextEligibleTurn = currentTurn + lag; prompt re-elicits the eligible objective that has waited longest; interleave so no objective is retrieved on consecutive turns. ENFORCE RETRIEVAL-BEFORE-DISPLAY (biggest correctness issue): first elicitation must hide targetSL (cue = scenario context + hintEN); a phrase shown in the Story can't count toward its retrieval quota until produced cold; takeaway/answer-key reveals only AFTER an attempt. STATE MACHINE: keep pending→recast→completed as display, but back with retrievalCount(0-3), lastSuccessTurn, and a strength score (cold success = 1.0, recast/echoed success = 0.5); completed at strength ≥3 with ≥2 successes at lag ≥2; a failed retrieval after a success DECREMENTS strength by 1 (detect within-session decay). CROSS-SESSION (net-new, highest cross-session value): per-learner-per-objective Leitner box + dueDate (box1→+1d, 2→+3d, 3→+7d, 4→+21d); each session PREPENDS 1-2 due objectives from prior scenarios (reuse shared id+audio = zero new content cost); correct cold review → promote box, fail → reset to box1.
SCENARIO RUBRIC: 3-5 objectives (≤4 novel items in flight; 5 only if 1-2 are reviews); ≥1 interleaved review objective from a prior scenario; ordering interleaves (no consecutive retrieval of same objective); every objective productively elicitable from context+hint alone; measurable (yields retrievalCount + lag, not just pass/fail); total available cold retrievals ≥ 3 × #objectives within the cap.
OBJECTIVE RUBRIC: success = unaided production from a context cue, answer hidden; mastered = 3 spaced successes, ≥2 at lag ≥2, ≥1 cold; has a decay signal (failed/aided production after success decrements + re-queues); hintEN targets a predictable error (calibrated desirable difficulty); reusable id+audio; tolerate trivial variation (else you measure recall of one string, not the skill).
SUFFICIENCY: gives the two things chit-chat fails at — forced retrieval + measurement. Gaps: (1) cross-session spaced review (net-new) — THE thing that makes it exceed messy in-person practice; highest impact. (2) retrieval-before-display (buildable). (3) strength/decay field + 3-retrieval rule (buildable). (4) expanding within-session spacing + interleaving (buildable). (5) acceptance tolerance beyond one string (net-new, small).
TOP MOVES: retrieval-before-display rule; 3 spaced cold successes + strength/decay field; cross-session Leitner (prepend 1-2 due items); interleave no-consecutive; variant tolerance.
COUNTER: optimizing retrieval of canonical phrases risks brittle, non-transferable strings (transfer-appropriate processing wants varied cues); "spacing a brittle representation just makes brittleness durable" — broadening acceptance + cue variability may matter MORE than perfecting the schedule.

[A5 — psycholinguist of speech production]
LOOP: move each chunk comprehension→cued production→free retrieval→TIMED retrieval, via 4 stations: (1) SEED phonological target — hear targetSL in native TTS twice (normal + chunked at word-group boundaries); never produce before a clean acoustic target exists or they encode L1-transferred phonology (English vowel reduction, wrong stress, devoiced finals). (2) PRACTICE = articulation reps (3-5) with SHADOWING — speak OVER the native audio, not after; listen for one feature at a time (stress → hard cluster → case ending). (3) cued production in the turn loop — use userVerbatim (not the gloss) diffed against targetSL to CLASSIFY failure: omission / L1-substitution / phonological slip / morphological slip; the correction names the type. (4) FLUENCY dimension (net-new lever): once correct once, re-elicit with a ~2s response-time target ("say it before the beat"); mark AUTOMATIZED only when correct AND within latency on a LATER turn; latency = button-press − prompt-audio-end. Freeze/code-switch in the prompt: stay Slovenian + short; on freeze (>3s) give the FIRST phonological chunk as a carrier ("Dober…?") not the whole answer; treat English insertion as attempted, recast only the inserted span.
SCENARIO RUBRIC: 4-6 objectives each sayable in ONE breath (≤7 syllables / ~1.5s); chunks share recurring frames (greetings, "I'd like…", numbers) so retrieval routines transfer; articulatory progression — early objectives phonologically easy (open syllables, no clusters), later ones add ONE new hard feature (cluster, č/š/ž, palatalization); phonological load front-loaded by hearing not reading; ≥1 chunk recurs ≥2x in-scenario; coherent transaction so chunks are cued by situation.
OBJECTIVE RUBRIC: ONE formulaic chunk stored/retrieved as a unit; ≤7 syllables, single intonation contour; introduces at most ONE new articulatory challenge; hintEN names the specific L1 interference; has a clear native acoustic model heard before producing; "produced" = correct form (trivial phonetic variation ok) AND, for mastery, within latency on a later turn; failure diagnosable from userVerbatim into a type.
SUFFICIENCY: for MECHANICS (lexical access speed, chunk retrieval, articulation) largely sufficient and exceeds chit-chat (unlimited rep, replayable model, verbatim diagnosis, no face-cost to freezing). Gaps: (1) speed/latency pressure — net-new, highest; buildable from existing timestamps. (2) pronunciation feedback on 1-2 known-hard phonemes — net-new. (3) cross-session spacing — net-new. (4) variant acceptance — net-new/buildable. (5) shadowing in practice — buildable now (content-only).
TOP MOVES: latency-gated mastery; userVerbatim failure-typing in the prompt; partial-cue recast on freeze; shadowing reps in practice; chunked native target before any production.
COUNTER: speed pressure before forms are stably accurate AUTOMATIZES errors (the opposite of the goal) and raises anxiety → narrows working memory → more freezing/code-switching; the accuracy prerequisite is only loosely verified without real pronunciation feedback.

[A6 — Slovene sociolinguist / pragmatics]
LOOP: the per-turn prompt anchors REGISTER FIRST. Café barista = tikanje (ti), pogovorni jezik (colloquial standard, not dialect, not formal knjižni), short elliptical turns ("Kaj bo?" not "Kaj bi želeli naročiti?"); never initiate vi unless the scenario is explicitly formal (upravna enota, doctor). Recast covers PRAGMATICS not just grammar: a grammatically-fine-but-unnatural learner line ("Bi radi kavo" to a barista) → tutor models the natural form ("Eno kavo, prosim"), correction = "More natural: direct object + prosim", never moralizing. Objectives ordered low→high pragmatic risk (greeting/order → complaint/repair/leaving). Story primes register: present tense, colloquial lexis, the dual where natural ("Sva dva"). REPRODUCIBLE AUTHORING RULE: every tutor prompt answers 3 questions FIRST — (1) ti or vi? (2) knjižni or pogovorni? (3) what's the SHORTEST turn a native would actually make here? — and that shortest-turn answer sets the model reply length.
SCENARIO RUBRIC: real transaction in the first 90 days (café, pekarna, supermarket checkout, zdravstveni dom, upravna enota); register specified & consistent (ti throughout a café, vi throughout an office); ≥1 greeting norm that surprises learners ("Dober dan" not "Zdravo" to a stranger; "Se vidimo"/"Nasvidenje" as a closing); ≥1 turn that naturally produces/hears the dual if two people are addressed ("za naju", "za dva"); NO textbook-but-never-said phrase ("Želim si skodelico kave"); final objective is a closing move in one breath ("Hvala, nasvidenje").
OBJECTIVE RUBRIC: targetSL is the phrase a native says, not what a grammar book generates (test: ask a Ljubljana resident, not a teacher — "Eno veliko kavo, prosim" passes; "Prosil bi za veliko kavo" fails as over-hedged); register tag explicit in the record (ti/vi, pogovorni/knjižni); hintEN names the specific error ("learners say 'Jaz bi rad'; natives drop 'jaz', often just 'Kavo, prosim'"); acceptable variants documented even if only one is scored ("Kavo, prosim" / "Eno kavo, prosim" both native); tests a pragmatic MOVE (greeting/order/check/closing) not vocabulary in isolation.
SUFFICIENCY (ranked): (1) register flexibility — buildable; teach when vi vs ti is obligatory; author parallel objectives in formal scenarios; tutor recasts a wrong-register form ("V tej situaciji rečemo 'vi'."). (2) pragmatic-move coverage (repair "Oprostite, nisem razumel/a", softeners, closing rituals) — buildable; chit-chat skips these. (3) the dual — buildable, low effort. (4) acceptable-variant sets with register tags ("Hvala" / "Hvala lepa" / "Najlepša hvala") — buildable, authoring cost. (5) dialect exposure ("cajt", "štacuna", "šalca") — net-new; a dialect-note field in takeaway.
TOP MOVES: tutor-prompt register declaration first; pragmatic recast in the correction field; the dual in story + ≥1 objective per multi-person scenario; acceptable-variants field in the objective record; a closing-move objective in every scenario.
COUNTER: over-specifying colloquial register → a learner casual in a café but catastrophically informal at a government office or with an elderly stranger; teaching register as a per-scenario SETTING rather than a live, responsive social judgment.

[A7 — conversation / voice-interface designer]
LOOP: every turn = detect channel health (compare userVerbatim vs userSaid) → act in character → return the floor. Three states: CLEAN (verbatim≈said, on-topic) → reply, advance, no confirmation (don't nag a turn that landed). MISHEARD/LOW-CONFIDENCE (garbled/empty/stretch) → repair IN CHARACTER with implicit-confirmation recast ("Kavo, ja?") that both confirms and models — a free repetition; never surface "ASR error" to a nervous learner. OFF-TOPIC/SILENCE → hold the floor with a NARROWING prompt / closed choice ("Kavo ali čaj?") that shrinks the ASR search space and rescues a frozen learner. PROMPT RULES: on verbatim/said divergence don't comment on hearing — recast the likely target as a short question, stay in role; max one clause (~3-7 words), always end by handing the floor back; never ask for a repeat in English; never grammar in tutorReply (UI-only); 2nd consecutive miss on an objective → drop to a binary choice containing the target word; silence → assume nervousness, offer the easier half as a model. LATENCY MASKING: keep tutorReply short so first-syllable TTS latency is low; play a tiny cached non-lexical backchannel ("Mhm"/"Ja…") locally while the model hop runs; show a thinking pulse on the button. PUSH-TO-TALK: hold-to-talk is right for a nervous learner (no endpointing/barge-in anxiety); add a visible hold timer/waveform; min-duration guard (<300ms tap → "hold and speak" coaching, not an empty turn); lock the button during the hop; one-tap re-send of the last recording on hop failure. SESSION: 14-cap = dead-end guard; if 3 turns pass with no objectiveProgress, seed the target more overtly; always end on the takeaway even if incomplete.
SCENARIO RUBRIC: no turn ends without returning the floor; no dead ends (every miss has an in-character recovery; cap guarantees clean exit); learner holds >50% of talk time (sum hold-duration vs TTS-duration; tutor turns ≤7 words); recovers from ASR noise (garbled/empty → recast, never an English "huh?"); first-TTS-syllable latency feels conversational; closed prompts available on stall, difficulty ratchets DOWN under failure; stays in character throughout.
OBJECTIVE RUBRIC: elicitable by a natural in-character line WITHOUT quoting targetSL; ASR-robust completion (doesn't hinge on one fragile phoneme — single-canonical-phrase acceptance is brittle); clean repair path (hintEN maps to a recast voiced as a question); a binary fallback prompt that embeds the target word; short to produce (one breath, clean endpointing).
SUFFICIENCY: as a channel, EXCEEDS messy in-person on (1) replay + cached audio — buildable, highest differentiator; (2) patience / no social cost of silence — buildable; (3) structure + guaranteed clean exit — buildable. Missing: (1) confidence-graded / fuzzy / semantic-equivalence acceptance — net-new, high; single canonical phrase is the weakest link (ASR variation false-rejects). (2) barge-in / open mic — net-new, medium; KEEP push-to-talk, don't chase early. (3) disfluency tolerance via prompt (ignore fillers/false-starts) — buildable. (4) real-time backchannel — cached token approximates cheaply.
TOP MOVES: verbatim-vs-said implicit-confirmation recast rule; instant ack token + thinking affordance; difficulty ratchets DOWN → binary closed choice on miss; fuzzy/semantic objective acceptance; push-to-talk guards.
COUNTER: a recast-everything reflex risks an infinite-confirmation loop if userSaid is systematically biased — the tutor "confirms" a phrase the learner never said and it feels like gaslighting; needs an occasional explicit low-shame "Še enkrat?" and a hard cap of one recast before advancing/seeding.

[A8 — behavioral / habit & motivation designer]
LOOP: preview = anxiety pre-loading, mandatory on first run, skippable on repeats; END the story on the tutor's literal opening line (desensitization — they've already "heard" what's coming). Session = 4-6 objectives, never >8 (goal-gradient needs a VISIBLE end; 14-cap maps to 5-6); target 7-10 min of speaking; leave them mid-appetite. Dots framed as "phrases you OWN," not "steps completed"; on each ◐→● a 0.5s targetSL highlight micro-beat (not fanfare); takeaway lists phrases in PRODUCTION order ("You said this," not "Completed"). Recast/failure FEEL: correction reads as orientation not judgment ("Slovenians say X here", not "incorrect"); ◐ signals in-progress not failed; tutor just continues — no apology loop; warmth without false praise ("Dobro, skoraj!"). END MOMENT: takeaway saveable/shareable one-tap; AUTO-PLAY one of the learner's OWN completed recordings (hearing yourself succeed > reading a list); one sentence: "You're ready for [next scenario]". CROSS-SESSION HOOK (no dark patterns): NO streaks; use Zeigarnik — leave one scenario visibly "started but not repeated"; captured runs show "N days ago"; optional opt-in GOAL reminder, not a streak; "next scenario unlocks" framing = arrival not obligation.
SCENARIO RUBRIC: completable in one sitting (<10 min speaking); a real recognizable transaction; a narrative arc (opening, small complication/choice, close); 4-6 objectives, none orphaned; first objective = lowest-stakes utterance (win immediately); final objective slightly harder (end on a stretch, not a coast); ≥2 objectives share phrases with other scenarios (familiarity = confidence transfer); story preview ends on the tutor's opening line.
OBJECTIVE RUBRIC: one canonical target ≤8 words; approximable on the first attempt even with imperfect Slovenian; failure recoverable in 1-2 recasts without threatening the cap; hintEN names the specific English-speaker error; completing it moves something visible (the dot); sounds like a real Slovenian line; new enough to feel like progress, familiar enough not to feel impossible.
SUFFICIENCY: (1) story preview removes the freeze moment — buildable. (2) replay (hear yourself/tutor succeed) — unavailable IRL — buildable. (3) no social judgment — biggest adherence driver; protect it in prompting. (4) MISSING pronunciation feedback — net-new, high. (5) MISSING a "real person moment" (occasional async native feedback / community clip) — net-new. (6) MISSING visible improvement history (run 1 vs run N of the same scenario; infra exists in captured runs) — buildable, underused.
TOP MOVES: auto-play the learner's own success recording at session end; story preview ends on the tutor's opening line; reframe dots as "phrases you own"; lock session max at 6 objectives; add run-comparison to the captured-runs UI.
COUNTER: the biggest retention risk is PLATEAU INVISIBILITY, not anxiety — without a cross-session model showing a trajectory, the app nails week 1 and loses week 2; everything else optimizes the single session but nothing yet closes the loop across weeks.

=== END EXPERT OUTPUTS ===

Produce a synthesis with EXACTLY this structure. Be decisive and concrete; the reader will implement this.

## Consensus
Points raised by 3+ experts (cite personas). The strongest, lowest-regret commitments.

## Genuine disagreements
The real judgment calls (not framing). For each: the positions + who held them + which has stronger reasoning, OR flag it as a call the builder must make. Cover at least: (a) production-first vs more comprehension/input early & correction intensity; (b) deterministic single canonical phrase vs accepted-variant/fuzzy acceptance; (c) speed/fluency pressure timing; (d) how much cross-session machinery to build now.

## High-value outliers
Single-expert insights worth surfacing (one line each on why it matters).

## The unified learning loop
A single concrete, reproducible loop (pre-session preview → per-turn → session-end → across-runs), naming which lever each step uses. Resolve overlaps (e.g. circling ladder + retrieval-before-display + verbatim-vs-said repair + forced-uptake + register-first prompt must coexist — show how). Make it implementable.

## Rubric — an excellent SCENARIO
A single merged checklist (dedupe the 8). Each item crisp and testable.

## Rubric — an excellent OBJECTIVE
A single merged checklist (dedupe the 8). Each item crisp and testable.

## Sufficiency verdict vs. in-person
Decisive answer: does the current feature set give the learner what they MOST need when in-person is unavailable/unstructured? Where it already EXCEEDS chit-chat, and the ranked gaps.

## Prioritized implementation backlog
A ranked list (highest impact × ease first). For each: one-line what, the lever it uses, BUILDABLE-NOW vs NET-NEW, and the expected effect. Separate "do now" (prompt/state-machine/authoring changes) from "net-new investments". This is the deliverable the builder acts on.

## Confidence
low/medium/high + one line, based on convergence vs split.

attachment.content:
- code-context: Spawn a subagent that returns two artifacts about the codebase as it relates to a user query — (1) an enriched, comprehensive high-level codebase map with extra detail in areas germane to the query, and (2) precise technical detail (function signatures, configuration options, schemas, algorithms) for the specific libraries/files most relevant to the query. The output is descriptive, not directive — it does NOT recommend solutions, advocate approaches, or reference the user's query in the prose. It hands the caller a map of the territory and a sharpened toolkit. When the caller already holds a canonical backdrop (repo map + schemas), it skips the map and returns only the sharpened technical reference scoped to the objective. Use when the user is starting non-trivial work that requires both general codebase awareness AND precise grounding in specific APIs, when the user explicitly asks for codebase context or "what do I need to know," or before drafting any plan/spec/migration that touches multiple subsystems. Do NOT use for narrow questions about a single function or for follow-ups in an already-grounded conversation.
- commit: Create structured git commits from current changes. Use when user says "commit", "save changes", or after finishing a feature.
- debug: Debug an error or unexpected behavior. Use when user mentions "bug", "error", "broken", "not working", "debug", or pastes an error message.
- deploy-check: Run pre-deployment checks. Use when user mentions "deploy", "ship", "release", or "production".
- docs: Generate or update documentation. Use when user mentions "docs", "documentation", "README", "JSDoc", or "comments".
- handoff: Produce a handoff brief that lets a future agent/session pick up the work without rediscovering what this session learned, and without re-reading what is already in the native environment. The skill triages every objective-relevant fact — native-environment info becomes a precise pointer, conversation-only info is written in full with evidence and confidence. Use when wrapping up a session, handing work to the next agent, or when the user says "handoff", "create handoff", "prep handoff for next session", or /handoff.
- migrate: Create a database migration. Use when user mentions "migration", "schema change", "add column", "create table", or "alter table".
- pr: Generate a PR description from current branch changes. Use when user mentions "PR", "pull request", or "merge".
- refactor: Refactor code while preserving behavior. Use when user mentions "refactor", "clean up", "simplify", or "restructure".
- review: Review code for bugs, security issues, and style violations. Use when reviewing PRs, checking code quality, or when user mentions "review", "PR", "code quality".
- security: Scan for security vulnerabilities. Use when user mentions "security", "audit", "vulnerability", "CVE", or before deployments.
- stochastic-multi-agent-consensus: Spawn N persona-driven agents to independently analyze a problem, then aggregate via a separate synthesis agent. Use for decision-making, ranking options, strategic analysis, or open-ended judgment where you want to filter hallucinations and surface high-variance perspectives. Triggers on "consensus", "poll agents", "stochastic consensus", "spawn N agents to analyze", "multi-agent vote", or /stochastic-multi-agent-consensus. Also triggers on "what do N agents think", "get multiple opinions", or "poll on [topic]".
- test: Write tests for a file or function. Use when user mentions "test", "tests", "coverage", or "spec".
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

This is a synthesis-writing task. The 8 expert outputs are fully provided in the prompt, and the deliverable is a written document with a fixed structure. No codebase investigation is needed — the material is self-contained. I'll write the synthesis directly.

## Consensus

Points held by 3+ experts — the lowest-regret commitments:

1. **Recast-then-forced-reproduction is the core mechanic.** Completion requires the learner to produce the corrected form on a LATER turn, not the same turn (A1, A2, A4, A5). Encode in the state machine: `recast` (◐) → `completed` (●) only after a post-recast unaided success.

2. **Tutor stays in character; correction is UI-only, never spoken.** The tutorReply is short Slovenian that hands the floor back; grammar/correction lives in the English UI field and is framed as orientation, not judgment (A1, A2, A3, A6, A7, A8). The world keeps moving whether or not the learner caught the grammar.

3. **Every tutor turn ends in an elicitation / leaves a gap** that makes the target the obvious answer — negotiation of meaning, not recitation (A1, A2, A5, A7). Max ~7-8 words per tutor turn (A1 "one short utterance", A2 "max 8 words", A6 "shortest turn a native would make", A7 "3-7 words").

4. **Story preview = comprehensible-input priming, Slovenian-only, no grammar, one frame per objective** (A1, A2, A3, A8). Mandatory first run, skippable on repeats.

5. **hintEN must name the ONE specific predictable English-speaker error**, not generic advice (A1, A2, A3, A4, A6, A8). This is repeatedly called the single most valuable thing the tool reliably does that human chit-chat does not (A3, A4).

6. **targetSL is a whole formulaic chunk doing a communicative job (2-6 words / ≤7-8 syllables), not a lemma or conjugation pattern** (A1, A2, A3, A5, A6). Test: a native actually says it; a grammar book generating it is a fail (A6).

7. **Accepted-variant sets, not a single brittle canonical string** (A1, A2, A4, A5, A6, A7). Near-unanimous. The single-canonical-phrase design is the most-cited weak link (false-rejects via ASR/word-order variation).

8. **Difficulty ratchets DOWN under failure** via a circling/narrowing ladder: open → either/or → binary choice embedding the target; on freeze, give the easier half / first chunk as a carrier, never the whole answer (A2, A5, A7). Cap at one recast before advancing/seeding to avoid loops (A7).

9. **Cross-session spaced review is the #1 ranked gap and the thing that would make the app EXCEED messy in-person practice** (A1, A4, A3, A8 all rank it top or near-top). Even a crude "seen N days ago → resurface as objective #1" beats nothing (A1).

10. **Session = 4-6 objectives, greeting→core→closing arc, 14-turn cap as a clean-exit guard; always end on the takeaway even if incomplete** (A1, A2, A3, A6, A7, A8). End on a communicative success the learner can picture doing tomorrow.

11. **Replay of cached native audio + the learner's own captured runs is the clearest already-built differentiator over in-person** (A2, A3, A7, A8): infinite patient repetition, no social cost of silence/freezing.

## Genuine disagreements

**(a) Production-first vs. more comprehension/input early; correction intensity.**
- *Push production + correction early:* A1, A2, A4, A5 build the whole loop around forced output and recast.
- *Input-primacy counter:* A1's own counter (Krashen) and A5's counter warn that correcting/pressuring accuracy too early raises anxiety, narrows working memory, suppresses willingness to communicate, and that the scarce resource (cheap native audio) might buy more as input. A3 echoes this (acquisition is also ambient).
- **Stronger reasoning / resolution:** Production-first wins *as the app's job* — pushed output + recast is precisely what unstructured chit-chat fails to guarantee, and that's the app's reason to exist. BUT honor the counter via *sequencing within a turn*: input precedes production (hear the chunk before producing it — A5's "seed acoustic target," A4's retrieval-before-display), and the FIRST objective is a guaranteed early win (A2, A8). Keep corrections low-shame and capped at one recast (A7). Net: production-first, input-front-loaded, correction gentle and bounded.

**(b) Single canonical phrase vs. accepted-variant/fuzzy acceptance.**
- *Keep deterministic single string:* the current build (and A4's note that variant tolerance is "small" impact relative to the schedule).
- *Broaden acceptance:* A1, A2, A5, A6, A7 — and A4's and A7's COUNTERS escalate this: "spacing a brittle representation makes brittleness durable" (A4); single canonical phrase is "the weakest link" causing false-rejects (A7).
- **Stronger reasoning:** Broaden acceptance — near-consensus, and the counters from the two most schedule/channel-focused experts make it decisive. **Builder call on mechanism:** an authored accepted-variant SET per objective (buildable now, deterministic, low risk) vs. semantic/confidence-graded fuzzy match (net-new, higher payoff, more risk). Recommend: ship the variant-set now, defer fuzzy.

**(c) Speed/fluency-pressure timing.**
- *Add latency-gated mastery now:* A5 (primary lever, buildable from existing timestamps), A1 (optional "second lap"), A2 (graduated recall).
- *Counter:* A5's own counter — speed pressure before forms are stably accurate AUTOMATIZES errors and raises anxiety; accuracy prerequisite is only loosely verified without pronunciation feedback.
- **Resolution:** Gate it. Latency pressure applies ONLY after a chunk has ≥2 accurate unaided successes, and only as an *optional* second-lap re-run, never on first contact. This is a deliberate, late lever — not in the v1 core loop.

**(d) How much cross-session machinery to build now.**
- *Full Leitner + dueDate + box promotion:* A4 (per-learner-per-objective boxes, +1/+3/+7/+21d).
- *Crude resurface-first:* A1 ("seen N days ago → objective #1"), A8 (Zeigarnik "started not repeated," no streaks), A3 (graduated scenario across runs).
- **Resolution:** Build the *minimal* cross-session hook now — persist per-objective last-success date + a due flag, and PREPEND 1-2 due objectives (reusing shared id+audio = zero content cost, A4). Defer the full 4-box scheduler and tuned intervals. This captures ~80% of the top-ranked gap at a fraction of the cost. **The one net-new investment everyone agrees is worth it.**

## High-value outliers

- **A5 — userVerbatim failure-typing:** diff raw ASR against targetSL to CLASSIFY the error (omission / L1-substitution / phonological / morphological) so the correction names the *type*. Turns the verbatim field into a diagnostic engine; buildable in the prompt.
- **A7 — verbatim-vs-said channel-health detection + cached backchannel token:** comparing the two ASR fields detects mishearing vs. off-topic, and a tiny local "Mhm"/"Ja…" masks model latency. Cheap, high realism.
- **A8 — auto-play the learner's OWN success recording at session end:** hearing yourself succeed beats reading a list; uses already-captured runs; strongest adherence lever named.
- **A6 — register declaration FIRST in every tutor prompt** (ti/vi? knjižni/pogovorni? shortest native turn?) as a reproducible authoring rule that also sets reply length. Prevents textbook-but-never-said phrasing.
- **A8 — story preview ends on the tutor's literal opening line** (desensitization): they've already "heard" turn one before it's live.
- **A6 — the dual** (Slovenian dvojina): author ≥1 objective per multi-person scenario; uniquely Slovenian, low effort, invisible to generic designs.
- **A4 — retrieval-before-display:** a phrase shown in the Story can't count toward its retrieval quota until produced cold; answer key reveals only after an attempt. Prevents recognition masquerading as recall.
- **A7 — anti-gaslighting cap:** hard limit of one recast before advancing, plus an occasional explicit low-shame "Še enkrat?" — guards against confirming a phrase the learner never said.

## The unified learning loop

A single reproducible loop. Levers named per step. The four big mechanics coexist as an ordered cascade *within each turn*.

**PRE-SESSION (preview) — lever: story preview, comprehensible input**
1. Auto-play the ≤5-sentence story, Slovenian only, one frame per objective, no grammar, no quiz (A1/A2/A3/A8). Mandatory first run, skippable on repeat.
2. Final frame ends on the tutor's literal opening line (A8 desensitization).
3. For any objective ≥4 syllables, offer optional practice-mode reps before going live (A1): hear canonical (normal + chunked at word-group boundaries, A5) → shadow over the audio → compare. Audio at NATURAL speed (A3).

**SESSION START — lever: cross-session prepend**
4. PREPEND 1-2 "due" objectives from prior scenarios (shared id + cached audio, zero new content; A4/A1). These are cold reviews.

**PER-TURN CASCADE — levers: register-first prompt → retrieval-before-display → channel-health repair → circling ladder → forced-uptake state machine**

The per-turn prompt resolves in this order so the four mechanics don't collide:

5. **Author/prompt sets register FIRST** (A6): ti/vi, pogovorni/knjižni, shortest native turn — this fixes tutorReply length (≤7 words) and persona.
6. **Elicit the focus objective without quoting targetSL** (retrieval-before-display, A4): the tutor's in-character line makes the target the obvious answer; the canonical string and answer key stay hidden until after an attempt (A1/A4/A7).
7. Learner holds-to-talk and produces. Model returns the per-turn object.
8. **Channel-health check on userVerbatim vs userSaid** (A7):
   - CLEAN → accept, advance, no nagging.
   - MISHEARD/low-confidence → implicit-confirmation recast in character ("Kavo, ja?") — confirms + models, never surfaces "ASR error."
   - OFF-TOPIC/SILENCE (>3-4s) → narrowing prompt / closed choice that shrinks the ASR space and rescues the freeze.
9. **Acceptance against the accepted-variant set** (A1/A2/A5/A6/A7), not one string. On a miss, **classify the error from userVerbatim** (A5: omission/L1-sub/phonological/morphological) → write the specific, named hintEN-style note to the *correction* field (UI-only, orientation-not-judgment tone; A6/A8).
10. **If wrong, ratchet difficulty DOWN one rung** (circling ladder, A2/A5/A7): open → either/or → binary choice embedding the target; on freeze, offer the first chunk as a carrier ("Dober…?"), never the whole answer. **Hard cap: one recast before advancing/seeding** (A7 anti-gaslighting).
11. **State machine** (A1/A2/A4/A5): `pending → recast(◐) → completed(●)`. ● requires an UNAIDED reproduction of the corrected form on a turn AFTER the recast. Back each objective with `retrievalCount`, `lastSuccessTurn`, and (recommended) a strength score where cold success counts more than echoed/aided success; a failed retrieval after a success decrements strength (within-session decay signal, A4). Interleave: don't retrieve the same objective on consecutive turns; re-elicit a completed objective once ~2 turns later as a graduated-recall check (A2/A4).
12. **Latency masking** throughout: short tutorReply + cached non-lexical backchannel while the model hop runs; button locked during hop; one-tap re-send on failure (A7).

**SESSION END — lever: takeaway + own-success replay**
13. At turn 10, prompt shifts to "we're finishing — guide remaining objectives to completion"; no new ground after turn 10 (A2). 14-cap guarantees a clean exit.
14. Takeaway lists phrases in PRODUCTION order, framed "phrases you OWN / you said this" (A8), full phrases with replayable audio (A1/A2), saveable/offline (A3).
15. **Auto-play one of the learner's own completed recordings** + one line: "You're ready for [next scenario]" (A8).
16. Any objective still ◐ at cap → flagged "say it once more" and becomes objective #1 on re-run (A1) AND is marked due in the cross-session store.

**ACROSS RUNS — lever: cross-session prepend + Zeigarnik**
17. Persist per-objective last-success date + due flag; promote/reset on cold review outcome (minimal Leitner; A4). Resurface due items as the prepended objectives in step 4.
18. Scenarios GROW across runs (run1 order, run2 add paying, run3 small talk; A3). Same objective can recur in a harder register (A3/A6).
19. Captured-runs UI shows "N days ago" and a run-1-vs-run-N comparison (A8 plateau-visibility). NO streaks; opt-in goal reminder only (A8).

## Rubric — an excellent SCENARIO

- [ ] One real bounded transaction the learner will face within ~2 weeks (café, pekarna, supermarket, zdravstveni dom, upravna enota), completable in one sitting (<10 min speaking, ≤14 turns).
- [ ] **Paper-testable:** a zero-Slovenian adult could complete it by following the prompt's circling logic alone.
- [ ] 4-6 objectives (≤4 novel items in flight; a 5th/6th only if it's a review), none orphaned.
- [ ] Clear open→complication/choice→close arc; first objective is the lowest-stakes utterance (early win), final objective is a slight stretch and a closing move in one breath ("Hvala, nasvidenje").
- [ ] Objectives ordered to mirror the REAL interaction (and by what breaks down first under stress), not a logical grammar sequence.
- [ ] Every objective is functionally elicitable by a natural in-character tutor line WITHOUT quoting targetSL; the tutor never has to lecture to elicit.
- [ ] ≥1 objective forces negotiation of meaning (clarification / quantity / substitution / repair), not pure recitation.
- [ ] ≥1 interleaved review objective shared (by id + cached audio) with another scenario.
- [ ] Register specified and held consistent (ti throughout a café, vi throughout an office); ≥1 greeting/closing norm that surprises English speakers; the dual appears where two people are addressed.
- [ ] No dead ends: every miss has an in-character recovery; the cap guarantees a clean exit; difficulty ratchets DOWN on failure.
- [ ] Learner holds >50% of talk time (tutor turns ≤7 words); never spoken English; completion never requires reading.
- [ ] ASR-robust: completion doesn't hinge on one fragile phoneme; closed-choice fallbacks available on stall.
- [ ] Story preview maps 1:1 to objectives and ends on the tutor's opening line.
- [ ] End state = a communicative success the learner can picture doing tomorrow; no textbook-but-never-said phrasing.

## Rubric — an excellent OBJECTIVE

- [ ] `targetSL` is one whole formulaic chunk a native actually says (2-6 words, ≤7-8 syllables, single intonation contour) doing a communicative JOB — not a lemma, conjugation pattern, or "understand X." Test: ask a Ljubljana resident, not a teacher.
- [ ] Completable in isolation (does not require a prior objective's output as its input); approximable on the first attempt even with imperfect Slovenian.
- [ ] High surrender/transfer value: reused across situations; shares recurring frames (greetings, "I'd like…", numbers) and ideally a shared id+audio.
- [ ] Introduces at most ONE new hard articulatory feature (cluster, č/š/ž, palatalization, case ending).
- [ ] `hintEN` names ONE specific, predictable English-speaker error (e.g. "beginners say 'kava'; it's 'kavo', accusative after 'bi'") — calibrated desirable difficulty, not generic advice.
- [ ] Has an **accepted-variant set** (e.g. "Kavo, prosim" / "Eno kavo, prosim"), with register tags, even if scored against the canonical; tolerates trivial phonetic / ±1 word-order variation.
- [ ] A clean native acoustic model is heard (normal + chunked) BEFORE any production.
- [ ] Elicitable by a single natural in-character line without quoting the target; has a binary fallback prompt that embeds the target word; a clean recast path voiced as a question.
- [ ] Register explicit in the record (ti/vi, pogovorni/knjižni).
- [ ] **Completion (●) = unaided production of the correct form, answer hidden, on a turn AFTER the recast.** Mastery (recommended) = ≥2-3 spaced successes, ≥1 cold; optional latency gate only after accuracy is stable.
- [ ] Yields measurable state (retrievalCount, lag, success/fail) and a decay signal (post-success failure decrements + re-queues), not just pass/fail.
- [ ] Completing it moves something visible (the dot, framed "a phrase you own"); failure is recoverable in ≤1-2 recasts without threatening the cap.

## Sufficiency verdict vs. in-person

**Verdict: YES — the current feature set already delivers the learner's MOST critical needs when in-person is unavailable, with ONE decisive exception (cross-session spacing) that is also the cheapest high-value thing left to build.**

The app's reason to exist is that unstructured chit-chat does *not* reliably provide: guaranteed pushed output, systematic recast-then-reuse, a named exact-error correction, and infinite patient replay. The current tools (per-turn LLM object, deterministic state machine, cached/replayable audio, captured runs, story, practice mode) deliver all four. That is a real edge, not parity.

**Where it already EXCEEDS in-person chit-chat:**
- Infinite, patient, replayable native audio and replay of the learner's own runs — impossible IRL (A2/A3/A7/A8).
- Zero social cost to silence, freezing, or repetition — the biggest adherence driver (A7/A8).
- A correction that names the *exact* predictable error every time — humans rarely do this reliably (A3/A4).
- Guaranteed structure, forced retrieval, measurement, and a clean exit (A4/A7).

**Ranked gaps (what in-person/structured instruction still has that the app lacks):**
1. **Cross-session spaced retrieval** — net-new, HIGHEST. Without it the app nails week 1 and loses week 2 (A8 plateau-invisibility; A1/A4/A3 rank it #1). Minimal version is cheap.
2. **Broadened acceptance** (variant set now / semantic-fuzzy later) — the single canonical string false-rejects and durably reinforces a brittle representation (A7/A4/A1/A2/A5/A6).
3. **Pronunciation feedback** on 1-2 known-hard phonemes (č/š/ž, stress, devoiced finals) — net-new; the accuracy prerequisite for fluency is otherwise unverified (A5/A3/A8).
4. **Fluency/automatization pressure** — net-new, gated behind stable accuracy; latency from existing timestamps (A5/A1).
5. **Productive recombination / off-script robustness** — the app optimizes the bounded transaction; a learner can ace ordering and still freeze when a real person answers off-script (A3/A1/A2 counters). Mitigate via elicitation-phrasing rotation and scenario variety.

## Prioritized implementation backlog

**DO NOW — prompt / state-machine / authoring changes (buildable with existing tools):**

1. **Forced-uptake completion rule** — ● only on unaided reproduction on a turn AFTER the recast. *Lever:* state machine. *Effect:* kills lucky single-turn completions; this is the core mechanic. BUILDABLE-NOW.
2. **Accepted-variant sets per objective** (authored, with register tags) — accept ±1 word-order + 2-3 alternates. *Lever:* objective record + acceptance check. *Effect:* eliminates the most-cited false-reject failure; stops reinforcing brittleness. BUILDABLE-NOW.
3. **Turn-policy prompt rewrite:** register-first declaration → ≤7-word Slovenian reply that always ends in an elicitation → never quote targetSL → recast in character → correction UI-only and orientation-framed. *Lever:* per-turn prompt. *Effect:* makes every turn negotiation-of-meaning and keeps the tutor in character. BUILDABLE-NOW.
4. **Retrieval-before-display:** hide canonical string + answer key until after an attempt; Story-shown phrases don't count cold. *Lever:* prompt + state machine. *Effect:* recall, not recognition. BUILDABLE-NOW.
5. **Circling ladder + one-recast cap + freeze carrier** as IF/THEN rules (open→either/or→binary; first-chunk carrier on freeze; advance after one recast). *Lever:* prompt. *Effect:* no dead ends, no infinite-confirmation loop, rescues freezes. BUILDABLE-NOW.
6. **Channel-health (verbatim-vs-said) implicit-confirmation repair** + **userVerbatim error-typing** writing the specific correction note. *Lever:* prompt. *Effect:* turns the two ASR fields into a diagnostic + graceful repair engine. BUILDABLE-NOW.
7. **Story preview ends on the tutor's opening line; mandatory-first/skippable-repeat.** *Lever:* story preview. *Effect:* removes the freeze moment cheaply. BUILDABLE-NOW.
8. **Session-end own-success replay + production-order "phrases you own" takeaway.** *Lever:* captured runs + takeaway. *Effect:* strongest adherence lever, uses existing capture. BUILDABLE-NOW.
9. **Authoring audit pass:** chunk-not-word, native-not-textbook (Ljubljana-resident test), one-named-error hintEN, register + the dual, ≤6 objectives, shared ids. *Lever:* scenario/objective authoring + rubrics above. *Effect:* raises content quality across the board. BUILDABLE-NOW.
10. **Practice mode: chunked native model + shadowing, natural speed.** *Lever:* practice mode. *Effect:* clean acoustic target before production, no slowed-speech motor habits. BUILDABLE-NOW.

**NET-NEW INVESTMENTS (ranked by impact × ease):**

11. **Minimal cross-session spacing** — persist per-objective last-success date + due flag; PREPEND 1-2 due objectives (reuse id+audio); promote/reset on cold review. *Lever:* objective store + session start. *Effect:* THE gap that makes the app beat week-2 attrition; ~80% of full-Leitner value at a fraction of cost. **Highest net-new priority.** NET-NEW.
12. **Run-1-vs-run-N comparison in captured-runs UI** + "N days ago" Zeigarnik surfacing, no streaks. *Lever:* captured runs. *Effect:* plateau visibility — closes the across-weeks loop. NET-NEW (light).
13. **Within-session strength/decay field** (cold=1.0, echoed=0.5; post-success fail decrements; ≥2 cold successes at lag≥2 for mastery; interleave no-consecutive). *Lever:* state machine. *Effect:* reliable mastery signal, detects within-session decay. NET-NEW (medium).
14. **Latency-gated fluency second-lap** (optional faster re-run; mark automatized only if correct AND within ~2s on a later turn, gated behind stable accuracy). *Lever:* timestamps + re-run. *Effect:* automatization without auto-reinforcing errors. NET-NEW (gated, later).
15. **Pronunciation feedback on 1-2 known-hard phonemes.** *Lever:* new scoring. *Effect:* verifies the accuracy prerequisite for fluency; biggest remaining true gap but highest build cost. NET-NEW (defer).
16. **Semantic / confidence-graded fuzzy acceptance** (after variant-sets prove insufficient). NET-NEW (defer).
17. **Full Leitner scheduler + tuned intervals** (+1/+3/+7/+21d, 4 boxes) — upgrade from #11 once the minimal version proves the loop. NET-NEW (later).

## Confidence

**High.** Strong convergence on the core loop, both rubrics, the sufficiency verdict, and the top backlog items (7+ of the 8 align on the load-bearing mechanics). The genuine disagreements are bounded and resolvable by *sequencing/gating* rather than choosing sides, and each expert's own COUNTER was used to set those gates. The only real builder judgment calls are the *mechanism* for broadened acceptance (variant-set vs. fuzzy) and *how much* cross-session machinery to ship first — both de-risked by starting with the cheaper buildable-now version.
